facts.statement: Labidiosuchus fossils were discovered at the Serra do Veadinho site in the Peirópolis municipality of Minas Gerais, Brazil.
facts.quote: It was found in Serra do Veadinho site, Municipality of Peirópolis of Minas Gerais State

facts.statement: The species was collected from the Serra da Galga Formation within the Bauru Basin.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Serra da Galga Formation (Bauru Group) in the Bauru Basin

facts.statement: Labidiosuchus lived during the late Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: which dates to the late Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: The genus existed between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Labidiosuchus is classified as an extinct genus of notosuchian crocodyliforms.
facts.quote: Labidiosuchus is an extinct genus of notosuchian crocodyliforms

facts.statement: The genus belongs to the parent group Ziphosuchia.
The genus is known solely from the holotype specimen DGM 1480-R.
facts.quote: Labidiosuchus is known only from the holotype specimen DGM 1480-R

facts.statement: The animal possessed a bizarre dentition and a lower jaw with a Y-shaped outline.
facts.quote: Labidiosuchus had a very bizarre dentition and its lower jaw had a Y-shaped outline

facts.statement: The preserved holotype specimen measures approximately 70.5 mm in length.
facts.quote: The preserved specimen has a length of about 70.5 mm

facts.statement: The genus is defined by unique traits, including small teeth located on the medial side of the anterior dentary.
facts.quote: Labidiosuchus is characterized by a unique combination of characters, including four autapomorphies (unique characteristics) such as the presence of small teeth on the medial side of the anterior portion of the dentary

facts.statement: The first pair of teeth projected forward and were larger than the rest.
facts.quote: The first pair of teeth is procumbent and larger than all others

facts.statement: The genus was first named by Kellner, Figueiredo, Azevedo, and Campos in 2011.
facts.quote: Labidiosuchus was first named by Alexander W. A. Kellner, Rodrigo G. Figueiredo, Sergio A. K. Azevedo and Diogenes A. Campos in 2011

facts.statement: The generic name combines Greek words for "forceps" and "crocodile".
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek labis meaning "forceps" or "tongs" and souchos meaning "crocodile"

facts.statement: The species name honors the community that protects the Peirópolis palaeontological site.
facts.quote: The specific name comes from the Latin amicus meaning "friend", in honor of the community that has helped to protect the palaeontological site at Peirópolis

facts.statement: Researchers cannot determine the feeding preferences or exact phylogenetic position of Labidiosuchus due to the incomplete fossil record.
facts.quote: Due to the incompleteness of the holotype, its feeding preferences or the exact phylogenetic position can't be determined with certainty
